explanation: Keep a size-k max heap of squared distances. Whenever the heap grows too large, remove its farthest star. Square roots are needed only for the final returned Euclidean distances, whose order is unrestricted.
timeComplexity: O(n log(k + 1)) time. Each star makes a bounded-heap update; extracting the retained stars adds O(k log(k+1)).
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary and output space. At most k+1 heap entries are live, plus k output entries.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: After each input star, the max heap contains the nearest k stars among those seen, or all seen stars if fewer than k. Adding a new star and removing the largest squared distance preserves this invariant. Squaring is monotone on nonnegative distances, so square roots of the retained values are the required distances.
walkthrough: For stars (2,0,0), (0,0,5) and (1,2,2), squared distances are 4,25 and 9. With k=2, remove 25 when the third star arrives. Return distances 3 and 2 in either order.
edgeCases: Equal-distance stars are still separate input entries.
k=0 gives an empty result when allowed by the input contract.
